review_scope: Engineering review of 50 archived method depictions: State/Operation identities, declared routes, descriptions, grouped blocks, and targeted property/unknown inspection. Source excerpts are navigation aids, not a new full-paper scientific verification. Historical acceptance is not changed.

findings.3--seq: End-group and attachment changes recur across adjacent States; second-adapter placement is paper clarified inside a depicted block. Preserve broad boundary and distinguish properties from diagram symbols.
findings.3p-seq: Adaptor and splint have different roles; restricted tail RT is not transcript-body cDNA synthesis. Immediate RNase H product differs from the downstream cDNA endpoint.
findings.clickseq: Addition caption hides RT plus termination. Need typed terminal features, reagent roles and explicit click-junction effect; retain grouped RT and final PCR boundaries.
findings.cp-rna-seq: Several chemical classes coexist in one mixture. Two output States after ligation describe components, not isolated fractions. Selection history differs from current terminal chemistry.
findings.rasl-seq: RNA is the template, ligated probes the DNA reporter. Depicted capture ordering differs from paper implementation; source summary must not certify an executable route.
findings.drop-seq: Hybridized RNA, barcode-bearing cDNA and sequence data are different boundary entities; pooled beads must not be represented as pooled intact droplets.
findings.smart-seq2: Supplied TSO versus copied handle; broad final repair/PCR/purification block. Library indices are not automatically early cell barcodes or UMIs.
findings.g-t-seq: Noun-labelled capture operation; bead reagent versus processed lysate; RNA and DNA remain separate until data integration. Shared origin is not a molecular barcode.
findings.indrop: Photorelease changes primer attachment without erasing droplet identity; intact-droplet pooling differs from content mixing. Broad synthesis block contains later recovery.
findings.scatac-seq-cell-index: Replicated well operations and intact-nucleus pooling. Well-index combinations carry attribution; preserve branch instances without pretending three illustrated wells are the plate size.
findings.atac-seq: Sample chromatin and adapter-loaded transposome share generic input links. Different participant roles; coupled cleavage/tagging is one event with several effects.
findings.chipmentation: Captured chromatin retains bead association through tagging. Same Tn5 mechanism does not make input selection or measurement equivalent to ATAC.
findings.dnase-seq-dnasel-seq: Extracted DNA endpoint is not automatically a complete sequencing library. Generic isolation block must not gain an invented affinity mechanism.
findings.faire-seq-sono-seq: Crosslink/phase-selection history matters; common names on a grouped source do not imply identical variant interfaces. Extraction scope needs to remain visible.
findings.damid: Distinct treatment/control samples, reagent production with unshown inputs, and separate sequencing branches joined only as data. No fake atom-balance requirement.
findings.aba-seq: Enzyme captions need actions; selected terminal DNA may have unresolved attachment. Do not invent release to make endpoint look complete.
findings.fcab-seq: Matched control and protected branches need distinct local bisulfite/PCR instances; base-response classes are not literal contiguous genomic sequence.
findings.mab-seq: Control routing is not a chemical reaction. Methylation and conversion effects must retain original modification classes and the meaning of C/T output.
findings.bsas: Bisulfite-derived amplicons, primers and transposome have distinct roles. Tagmentation of amplicons is not chromatin-accessibility selection.
findings.methyl-seq-mre-seq: Physical split differs from data comparison. A prepared MRE fragment State can express an input boundary but cannot silently stand for drawn missing operations.
findings.hi-c-3c-seq-capture-c: Contact association becomes a junction. Grouped shared route does not specify each method's internal capture/amplification; relationship-specific refinement needed.
findings.chia-pet: Retained junction product and detached flanks differ; joint molecular contact may be represented by one complex State without replacing the ligation Operation.
findings.ng-capture-c: DNA repair/library, bait reagent and capture support are distinct; broad endpoint does not automatically establish release from beads.
findings.clash-seq: Two RNA partners may begin as one complex State; ligation changes covalent association and RT changes the carrier. No need to force one node per molecule.
findings.hiclip: Adaptor A and B roles/end blocks differ; linking preserves partner attribution. Final same-RNA/different-RNA classes are data categories, not material fractions.
findings.4sudrb-seq: Label cohort, chemical tagging and affinity selection differ; short glyphs do not demonstrate fragmentation. Supplied analog is not the measured target.
findings.bru-seq: Antibody-coated bead caption represents capture; pulse selection does not yield exact RNA birth time. Schematic fragmentation placement needs source qualification.
findings.bruchase-seq: Chase changes cohort age/composition without introducing a new barcode; temporal interpretation differs from current molecular state.
findings.mince-seq: Paper captures purified biotinylated DNA where drawing shows chromatin; resolved chemistry cannot leave contradictory endpoints presented as execution-ready.
findings.catch-it: Labelled protein is not sequenced DNA; association through histone-DNA complex carries the measurement. Removed proteins are material output distinct from retained DNA.
findings.icshape: Modification, click tagging and RT stop encode different effects. Bound RNA/cDNA complex and eluted cDNA need distinct carrier/attachment descriptions.
findings.shape-map: Mutation-bearing cDNA, reads and mutation profiles differ; reference sequence is a data input. Parallel depicted routes must not be silently mixed.
findings.cirs-seq: Two reagent branches with uncertain upper-lane label. Evidence-supported inference must remain distinguishable from an explicit legend.
findings.frag-seq: Several unlabelled carry-forward arrows produced extra operations. Require a supported action or unresolved/composite interface, not an invented transformation for every arrow.
findings.pseudo-seq: Two distinct size selections (RNA and cDNA) share a name; circularization changes DNA topology and supports later PCR.
findings.2b-rad: Restriction tag, ligated adapter and PCR-introduced sample barcode are different changes. Reagent role and attribution stage are essential.
findings.ddradseq: Diagram sequence conflicts with original double-digest ordering. Nonblocking schematic qualification must block later use as a verified executable order.
findings.hyrad: One DNA preparation becomes a probe reagent for a different sample library. Roles depend on operation, not permanent State type or molecular species.
findings.rapture: Nested well/plate pooling changes attribution levels; preserve independent preparations and later mixing without collapsing same-labelled repeated operations.
findings.smmip: Genomic DNA noun caption hides probe hybridization. Reporter circles differ from genomic target; tag families and consensus are data, not additional molecules.
findings.repli-seq: Shared-looking RNA/DNA labels cannot define analyte identity. Sorting and lysis are composite; final glyph dropping label does not establish chemical removal.
findings.guide-seq: Integrated DSB tag and later molecular-index adapters serve different identities; capture/enrichment is not a census of every cellular break.
findings.bless: Proximal and distal linker additions differ in purpose and position; retained and uncaptured fractions require distinct output interpretation.
findings.duplex-sequencing: Addition is distinct from ligation in this drawing; paired original strands become data families, then joint data consensus. No material pooling inferred from data join.
findings.safe-seqs: End-based identifiers can carry identity without random barcode chemistry. Broad solid-phase block has a genuine unresolved capture mechanism.
findings.net-seq: Protein target/complex, recovered nascent RNA and copied DNA are different entities; endpoint cDNA does not justify adding unseen sequencing settings.
findings.mnet-seq: Protected RNA selection and terminal phosphorylation matter; broad recovery need not be expanded into every cleanup operation.
findings.ribo-seq-art-seq-gti-seq: Depletion changes population composition; two extraction operations are distinct local occurrences. Grouped preparation does not prove all biological targets identical.
findings.pal-seq: Both sequence data and fluorescence data arise from persistent physical clusters. An operation can output material and data; observation need not consume its sample.
findings.tail-seq: End phosphorylation and tail information retained while bead release timing remains unknown. Missing attachment evidence cannot be filled by automatic carry-forward.

decisions: Keep the five internal Flow kinds; represent participant roles as separately evidenced annotations on declared input connections.
State properties use fixed facets with open source-supported values; omitted facet means not recorded, never absent or unchanged.
Operation effects bind exact input/output State groups without asserting all-to-all molecular derivation.
Record whether outputs are distinct products/fractions or coexisting components; collections and mixtures are allowed States.
Keep source grouping; record composite/unresolved boundary resolution. Expand only for a specific paper-supported comparison or consequential ambiguity.
Cross-method history/correspondence remains a reviewed claim anchored to operations and boundary context, not a material Flow or global State merge.
Existing contradictory schematic versus paper ordering remains a qualification to resolve before any executable-protocol claim. Do not silently repair archives.
